title: The enigma of Trump
gist: Partial (paywalled) mailbag: Yglesias argues Trump's motives remain opaque — indifferent yet fanatical on tariffs and immigration, disengaged from the Iran war he started, and seemingly indifferent to the midterm losses he helped cause. He predicts a 2028 GOP outsider will be 'post-Trump' rather than anti-Trump; text cuts off at the paywall.

insights.claim: Early ballot drops from Hamilton County, Indiana on 2026 midterm night proved an accurate leading indicator of national trends, despite analysts' caveats.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Early suburban county returns can be a fast read on national swing on election nights.

insights.claim: Yglesias says that despite overexposure and heavy reporting, Donald Trump's real priorities remain mysterious, unlike a legible politician such as Paul Ryan.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Policy forecasting for the remaining Trump term carries high uncertainty; avoid overconfident reads of his intentions.
insights.quote: Donald Trump is such an incredibly overexposed figure that it’s easy to overlook how mysterious he is.

insights.claim: Trump appears both indifferent (interested in money and construction projects) and borderline fanatical about tariffs and immigration, while rarely discussing immigration policy in detail.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Tariffs remain the area where Trump's commitment looks most durable — relevant for trade-exposed assets.
insights.quote: But he sometimes seems borderline fanatical about tariffs and immigration.

insights.claim: Trump gambled his presidency on a war with Iran yet seems largely disengaged from it.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Disengagement on the Iran war adds uncertainty to its trajectory and energy-market implications.
insights.quote: He gambled his presidency on a war with Iran but seems largely disengaged from it.

insights.claim: In Trump's first term apparent openness to bipartisan deals usually collapsed, though the CARES Act did get done — suggesting post-midterm deals with Democrats are possible but unreliable.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Divided-government deal prospects (e.g., spending, permitting) should be discounted but not ruled out.

insights.claim: After the midterm losses Trump seemed almost indifferent, despite having personally driven House redistricting fights and hand-picking disastrous Senate candidates in Texas and South Carolina.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Lowers near-term risk of post-election contestation; underscores Trump's candidate choices as a GOP liability.
insights.quote: He hand-picked disastrous Senate candidates in Texas and South Carolina.

insights.claim: A reader asks whether JD Vance and Marco Rubio remain the likeliest 2028 GOP nominees given midterm results discrediting the Trump administration.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: The midterm wipeout opens the 2028 GOP field.

insights.claim: Yglesias predicts a viable outsider 2028 Republican candidacy will come from a 'post-Trump' figure rather than an 'anti-Trump' figure.
insights.speaker: Matthew Yglesias
insights.so_what: Watch for GOP candidates who move past Trump without repudiating him; anti-Trump Republicans are unlikely to win.
insights.quote: My best guess is that a viable outsider candidacy won’t come from an “anti-Trump” figure but from someone I’d call a post-Trump figure.
